title: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland

lead.label: Overview
lead.text: In 1900, Victoria was sovereign and the Marquess of Salisbury was prime minister. Great Britain and Ireland shared a United Kingdom Parliament; the franchise remained restricted.

organization.label: Entity type
organization.text: United kingdom governed as a constitutional monarchy.

organization.label: Government
organization.text: Victoria was sovereign; Salisbury headed the government during his 1895–1902 premiership.

organization.label: Institutions
organization.text: The House of Commons and House of Lords formed the two parliamentary chambers. The monarch’s political influence operated within the developing constitutional system.

organization.label: Administrative relationships
organization.text: Ireland participated in the United Kingdom Parliament following the 1801 union. This domestic union is distinct from the empire’s varied overseas relationships.
organization.scope: 1900; imperial dependencies are not catalogued here

changes.text: Franchise reform and redistribution changed parliamentary representation; women remained excluded from parliamentary voting.
War began in South Africa and became a major issue for Salisbury’s government.

population.label: Population reference
population.text: 32,249,200 people: ONS mid-1900 estimate for England and Wales only. This is neither the full UK total nor a population at the clicked point.
population.scope: Mid-1900; no exact day asserted; England and Wales

overview.label: Crown, government and Parliament
overview.text: Victoria’s reign saw direct political authority move away from the sovereign, while the monarchy retained influence. In 1900 Salisbury was prime minister. The two parliamentary chambers remained central institutions, but political participation was far from universal.

overview.label: The union and its limits
overview.text: The union took effect in 1801, ending the separate Irish Parliament and bringing Irish representation to Westminster. This explains the historical title Great Britain and Ireland. It must not be replaced by the present-day United Kingdom’s name or boundaries.
